rendered: The question's premise does not match the paper. The paper does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich cathodes; it concludes the opposite. Its conclusion reads: "Overall, this work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]" The leaching data are the basis for that claim. The paper says the percentage of leached lithium increases with nickel content, but that even the Ni-rich cathode shows only minimal lithium leaching, about ~3 wt%[2] after a full week in water. XRD, Raman and XPS showed no bulk structural change and only minor surface changes. The paper also notes that the aqueous-processed NMC 811[3] cells have slightly lower capacity retention than NMP-processed cells but still cycle very well, and that formulation tweaks could improve them further.
